correctness.rationale: In the Klein disk hyperbolic geodesic segments are straight Euclidean chords, the central radius-a ball becomes a disk of Euclidean radius tanh(a), and an endpoint of radius r has tangent half-angle ψ_a(r)=acos(tanh(a)/tanh(r)). For two endpoints with smaller uniform angle Δ∈[0,π], crossing happens iff Δ>ψ_a(r)+ψ_a(s). The radial density is sinh(r)/(cosh(b)-cosh(a)); averaging yields P=1-2/[π(cosh b-cosh a)]∫_a^b sinh(r)ψ_a(r)dr. Integration by parts with u=sqrt(cosh²r-cosh²a) yields J=cosh b ψ_a(b)-atan(u/sinh a). Stochastic monotonicity of sampled r proves P strictly decreases b; expansion ψ_a(a+u)~sqrt(2u/(sinh a cosh a)) gives 4/(3π) thin-width coefficient; bounded convergence gives 2asin(tanh a)/π at b→∞. Independent 45-digit quadrature agrees at (a,b)=(0.5,1.5),(1,2),(0.3,7), probabilities .4224498703602261,.6436635619879831,.18846024259184707. The proof concerns ambient minimizing geodesic and area sampling, not Liouville sampling or annulus-intrinsic path.
